newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iran leader calls on summit defend Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Iran leader calls on summit defend Jerusalem.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani urged Moslem countries at an Istanbul summit on Sunday to oppose a U.S. House of Representatives' call on President Bill Clinton to reaffirm Jerusalem as Israel's "undivided capital".

Rafsanjani was speaking at a summit of the Developing-Eight (D-8) group, following the House's call that Clinton recommit himself to a 1995 law declaring Jerusalem Israel's capital and saying the American embassy should be moved there by May 1999.

"The decision to transfer the embassy from Tel Aviv to Al-Quds (Jerusalem) requires appropriate reaction from the Islamic world and from this forum of countries encompassing the majority of the Moslem population worldwide," he said.

"This constitutes a flagrant violation of the inalienable right of the Palesitinian people, and a further irrefutable indication of unjustifable American bias, which automaticaly disqualifies the United States from mediating the Palestinian crisis," Rafsanjani said at the opening of the summit .
The D-8 summit was attended by the presidents of Indonesia, Iran and Turkey, the prime ministers of Bnagladesh, Egypt Malasia and Pakistan and Nigeria's industry minister.
Israel, which captured Arab East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community including the United States, welcomed last week's House vote.
The House voteis not binding on the Clinton administration.
The Palestinians, who regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state, have termed the resolution a declaration of war.
The D-8 countries are meeting to sign a joint declaraiton later in the day. It was not known if the declaration would mention the matter of U.S. embassy.
The declaration is expected to call for moves to overcome trade barriers and establish joint business councils between member countries.
